Apple has filed its opposition to OpenAI's motion to dismiss the trade secrets lawsuit the company filed against two former employees, as well as OpenAI and io Products. Details below.

Some background

A few days ago, OpenAI filed a motion to dismiss the trade secrets lawsuit Apple filed against the company, io Products, Chang Liu, and Tang Tan.

In its request, OpenAI argued that Apple filed the lawsuit "without adequate investigation" and further set forth its version of events that allegedly led to Apple filing suit.

OpenAI's opposition was centered on three main points: that Apple "fails to demonstrate it owns protected trade secrets," that it "fails to allege conduct sufficient to support a trade secret misappropriation claim," and that it "fails to reasonably allege any harm or ongoing injury."

For example, OpenAI claimed that contrary to Apple's allegations, former Apple employee Chang Liu responded to consulting requests from a former colleague after leaving the company, rather than accessing Apple information without authorization, while former Apple VP Tang Tan retained Apple offboarding documents to help ensure new employees followed its security procedures.

The company also argued that Apple's own information management and offboarding practices were at fault, claiming Apple encouraged employees to use personal iCloud accounts for work and failed to properly cut off their access to company data after they left.

"Apple's lawsuit targets specific individuals stealing specific Apple trade secrets in specific ways"

Today, Apple filed its opposition to OpenAI's motion to dismiss, breaking down OpenAI's arguments point by point and claiming that "in short, Defendants fail to substantively respond to the egregious allegations at the core of the Complaint."

Apple argued that its original complaint "adequately identifies the specific trade secrets misappropriated by Defendants," and cited past cases in which courts found similar levels of detail sufficient to allow trade secret claims to proceed.

Apple also claimed OpenAI's argument that Apple failed to adequately protect its trade secrets was "equally unavailing," adding that OpenAI "dismisses Apple's trade secrets as mere 'vendor relationships,' then questions whether all 'vendor relationships' are confidential."

The company further argued that OpenAI is also misusing the dismissal mechanism as a whole. From the filing:

In its opposition, Apple also directly addressed a heavily redacted conversation OpenAI published on its website involving a former colleague who still works at Apple reaching out to Chang Liu to clarify certain information about an Apple project.

OpenAI argued that conversation proves Apple is being misleading in describing Liu's post-departure access to information as theft, because Apple employees themselves also reached out to him for information.
